_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401915380.overall: Bodø/Glimt are 25th of 36 with 4 points, both earned at home (1-0 against Dortmund, 0-0 against Lille), so this game on the Aspmyra artificial pitch is close to a must-win for the play-off places; they lead the Norwegian league and have won 14 of their last 15 league games. LASK are 16th with 6 points and arrive on five straight league wins, but vice-captain Andrés Andrade (ankle) is out, and the numbers now count him (+6.2% on Bodø's goals). Florian Flecker (calf), one of LASK's joint top Champions League scorers, is also out and is still not counted; Bello and Harakaté are out and counted, as are Evjen (knee) and Mikkelsen (groin) for Bodø. Line-ups are due an hour before kick-off and the match-day previews still show the same expected XIs as this morning, with Usor up front for LASK and Hauge and Blomberg wide for Bodø. Turkish referee Halil Umut Meler, whose higher card rate is already counted, is in charge on a cold night under floodlights.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals (2.9 Bodø, 1.1 LASK); since this morning they also count Andrade's absence (+6.2% for Bodø), plus LASK's hot scoring run (+2.8%) and Evjen, Mikkelsen and Bello. What they still cannot see is Flecker, one of LASK's main Champions League scorers, missing from every predicted XI, and Bodø's two home games in this competition produced one goal in total. I keep -4%, about 3.8 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, 5.9 of them for Bodø as the side expected to have the ball, with both teams' recent corner counts (+0.8% and -1.0%) already in. LASK's 3-5-2 with wing-backs Jørgensen and Dibango and Bodø's wide attack through Blomberg and Hauge are both confirmed in today's predicted line-ups, which is what the numbers expect, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already adding referee Halil Umut Meler's 4.5 cards a game (+7.5%) and taking off LASK's low recent card count (-6.6%) and Bodø's (-2.1%). There is no rivalry; a reshuffled LASK back three without Andrade on a fast artificial pitch, which Kühbauer calls an extra challenge, may be stretched a little, but that is a normal away-team picture, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots (14.4 Bodø, 12.5 LASK), already trimmed for Bodø's quieter recent shooting (-3.9%). Bodø need the win and will push, while Kühbauer says LASK want to take something home and will still play two strikers without Flecker; these pull both ways, so I stay at 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already counting LASK's sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and Bodø's slight dip (-2.0%). The LASK absences (Andrade at the back, Flecker up front) roughly cancel for shots on target, and I have put the net effect into goals rather than counting it twice, so I stay at 10.5.

401915300.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9; Galatasaray have won their last two Champions League games (Lille, Stuttgart) and want a top-24 place, while Villa lost 3-0 at Barcelona last time and Emery admits a top-8 finish is out of their hands. Osimhen, Leão and Sallai are out and the numbers count all three on goals; Sporx's match-day page still lists Osimhen as injured, with Jakobs a doubt, and the predicted XIs have no recognised centre-forward: Barış Alper Yılmaz, Yunus Akgün and Batrakov in attack with Lemina beside Torreira. Villa are without Cash, Ruggeri and Onana (all counted); Lindelöf was a doubt with illness, so Harwood-Bellis is expected alongside Pau Torres. Line-ups come an hour before kick-off and nothing has changed since this morning. German referee Daniel Siebert, average on cards and already counted, is in charge on a repaired RAMS Park pitch.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (1.1 Galatasaray, 1.8 Villa) and already take off Osimhen (-10%), Sallai and Leão (-5% each) from Galatasaray's goals, plus Cash for Villa. The striker-less plan is just the other side of Osimhen's absence; one report says he might sit on the bench, but at most for a late cameo, so nothing new moves the total and I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's slight rise in corners won (+2.9%) and Villa's dip (-3.4%). Villa keep the ball and push wide with Maatsen and Wan-Bissaka, while Galatasaray lose width without Leão and Sallai and, in today's Turkish line-ups, play Lemina in a more solid midfield; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-8.4%), Villa's slight rise (+3.7%) and Daniel Siebert's average record (4.1 a game, +1%) already in. RAMS Park is loud and both sides need points, and a patched pitch can bring a few clumsy challenges, but that is close to a normal Champions League night here, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots (12.8 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa); they take the missing forwards off goals but not off shots. With Osimhen, Sallai and Leão all out, no centre-forward in the predicted XI and Lemina added as a second holding midfielder, Galatasaray lose their main shot-takers, and a repaired pitch may slow the game; I keep the trim, to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+5.9%) and Galatasaray's slight dip (-0.8%), but not the forwards Galatasaray are missing. Osimhen is the player who turns their chances into efforts on target and he will not start, so I keep my lean lower, to about 9.7.

401915295.overall: Arsenal are 3rd in the league phase on 10 points and top of the Premier League despite Saturday's 2-2 draw at Newcastle; Dortmund are 12th on 9 points and top of the Bundesliga. Match-day previews confirm David Raya is out with the shoulder he hurt at Newcastle (no surgery needed), so Kepa starts in goal, and Zubimendi (hamstring) and Saka (quad) are also out; the numbers count Saka (about -10% on Arsenal's goals) and Raya, but not Zubimendi. Sports Mole expects Gyokeres, White, Hincapie and Lewis-Skelly back in the XI, with Saliba still not fit to start. For Dortmund, Emre Can, Inacio, Konstantelias, Lerma and Kaba are out; Guirassy is in the squad but UEFA still lists him doubtful with a thigh problem, so Fabio Silva or Beier is expected to lead the line. Italian referee Maurizio Mariani, slightly below average on cards, is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals; they already take about 10% off Arsenal for Saka and add a little to Dortmund for Raya's absence. Arsenal also miss Zubimendi's control in midfield, which the numbers don't count, and Dortmund have Guirassy available at least from the bench, so I stay a touch higher: 2.5 x 1.02, about 2.55.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Arsenal around 6.3 and Dortmund's busier recent corner count already in (+3.0%). Arsenal build corners from sustained pressure and set pieces even without Saka, with Madueke and Eze expected wide, and Dortmund tend to defend deep away in a back three; both records already show this, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, already adding about 13% to Arsenal for their high recent card count and trimming a little for Maurizio Mariani, who averages 3.9 cards a game against a 4.1 average. There are no bans and no needle between the clubs, so nothing new points either way; I stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Dortmund's busy recent shooting already counted (+11.3%) and Arsenal's (+5.7%). Gyokeres is expected back up front for Arsenal, but they still miss Saka's output on the right and Zubimendi's control, while Guirassy is at best a substitute for Dortmund. These roughly cancel, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, including a small boost for Dortmund's recent accuracy (+2.7%). Guirassy, Dortmund's most clinical finisher, is still listed doubtful and likely starts on the bench, and Arsenal have been less incisive without Saka, so nothing clearly moves it; I stay at 8.6.

401915296.overall: Como are 4th on 9 points in their first Champions League season and beat Cagliari 2-0 on Saturday; AEK are 29th on 3 points and need a result. Kean, Diao, Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are out for Como, but today's previews (UEFA, The Stats Zone) list Caqueret only as a doubt rather than out, Chalobah is fit again and Fabregas is expected to field Da Cunha, Nico Paz and Baturina behind Douvikas, so Como's attack looks stronger than it did this morning. The numbers take a little off for Diao and Kean and ride Como's 17 goals in six games. AEK travel without the suspended Koita and Zubkov (Arriaga is listed out by UEFA, though one preview still has him in the XI), and Fabregas calls them physical and dominant. Spanish referee Javier Alberola Rojas, who has averaged about 4.7 yellows a game this season, is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already trimming Como for Diao and Kean while adding 4.3% for their recent scoring. Caqueret is now only doubtful and Nico Paz, Baturina and Da Cunha are expected to start, so I soften this morning's -5; what is left is Como without natural wingers and AEK without Koita, a UEFA ban the numbers don't know about: 2.9 x 0.97, about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Como around 5.6 and both sides' small recent dips already in. Without natural wingers Como's width comes from full-backs Valle and Couto, who already supplied much of it, and AEK are likely to defend deep away from home; nothing clearly moves the count, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already take about 16% off Como for how few cards they have picked up lately, plus 7% off AEK. Alberola Rojas has shown about 4.7 yellows a game this season, a little busier than average, and Fabregas calls AEK physical, but the referee's record and AEK's style are already in the numbers, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Como are still short of forwards (Kean, Diao, Addai and Rodriguez out) and AEK lose Koita, one of their most frequent shooters, whom the numbers still count; with Paz and Baturina expected to start I keep the trim small: 25.4 x 0.98, about 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Como's sharp recent finishing counted. Koita's ban removes much of AEK's threat from wide, which the numbers don't see, and Como rely on Douvikas alone up front, though their creative midfielders are fit, so I go slightly lower: 9.3 x 0.97, about 9.0.

401915294.overall: Both sides have 3 points: Feyenoord are 32nd and Porto 26th, and both need wins to stay in the race for the top 24. Feyenoord are six games without a win after Saturday's 3-2 home defeat to Excelsior and have conceded eight in their last two league games, leaving Giovanni van Bronckhorst under pressure; Hadj Moussa is in the predicted XI after an ankle knock, but centre-back Watanabe is a doubt with a foot problem (not in the numbers), and St. Juste, Bos, Nieuwkoop, Beelen and Moder are out, St. Juste already counted. Porto lead the Portuguese league by five points, unbeaten in 11, and beat Napoli 4-1 last time out in Europe; Smalling is not in their Champions League squad and William Gomes is back in training but uncertain. Farioli expects a physical game with many duels and wants to press high. Bosnian referee Irfan Peljto, who gives fewer cards than average over his career, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already add a little to Porto for St. Juste's absence. Two sides who both need a win, a Feyenoord defence that has leaked eight in two league games and may also lose Watanabe, and a Porto side planning to press high point to an open game: 2.9 x 1.03, about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Feyenoord's lower recent count already in (-4.0%). Feyenoord usually have most of the ball at home and Hadj Moussa's dribbling helps them win corners, while Porto's full-backs push high; that is in both normal records, so I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and count Irfan Peljto's low card rate (-9.2%) and both sides' calm recent discipline. Farioli expects a physical game full of duels, which could add a booking, but Peljto lets a lot go over his career, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already add about 13% to Porto for how many shots Feyenoord have been conceding. Both teams must chase a win and Porto want to win the ball high, which tends to create quick shots on both sides: 26.3 x 1.02, about 26.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, including a 12.6% boost for Porto from Feyenoord's poor recent defending and a 4.7% cut for Feyenoord's poor finishing. With Hadj Moussa expected to start and Porto in form in front of goal, in a game both need to win, I go slightly up: 9.6 x 1.02, about 9.8.

401915379.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points but come in on four Premier League games without a win after Saturday's 1-1 home draw with Fulham, with Arsenal away on Sunday; Maresca wants a top-eight finish. Only Semenyo is out (already counted) and Matheus Nunes is fit again; today's previews expect only limited rotation, with Haaland, Doku and Cherki starting and Khusanov at right-back. Allegri's Napoli, 27th on 3 points, are without Buongiorno (meniscus), Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Meret, Badiashile, Vergara and Alisson Santos, and Rafa Marin is suspended, leaving Rrahmani and Beukema as the only fit specialist centre-backs; reports differ on whether Neres is fit. The numbers count Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Vergara and Rafa Marin but not Buongiorno. Romanian referee Istvan Kovacs, an average carder, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already take off for Semenyo, Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Vergara and the suspended Rafa Marin. They do not know Buongiorno is also out, leaving Napoli with two fit specialist centre-backs against Haaland, and today's previews expect City to rotate less than feared this morning, so I go a little further: 3.4 x 1.05, about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, mostly City's, and already add about 10% for how many corners Napoli have conceded lately. With a patched-up defence Napoli should be pinned back even more than their record shows, and blocked crosses from Doku and Ndiaye turn into corners: a mild lean up, to about 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Napoli's busier recent card count (+12%) and Istvan Kovacs's average record included, so I do not lean on the referee. What is left is a stand-in Napoli back line, likely with Politano at right-back, chasing City's wingers and likely to give away fouls: a small lean up, to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add about 13% to City for the volume Napoli have been allowing. Buongiorno's absence is not in that figure, and with Haaland, Doku and Cherki expected to start City should have even more of the ball, so I go up a bit more than this morning: 28.6 x 1.04, about 29.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with Napoli's sharp recent finishing (+8%) already counted. A weakened Napoli back line should let City shoot from closer in, and City's attack is expected near full strength, though they managed little against Fulham, so I keep the move small: 10.4 x 1.04, about 10.8.

401915299.overall: RB Leipzig (30th) and Lens (33rd) both have 3 points from four games and need a win to stay in the race for the top 24; Leipzig are 4th in the Bundesliga under Martin Demichelis after a 5-1 win at Union Berlin, Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in Didier Digard's first game after the 9-1 loss at Como. Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba (bruised knee) missed the final training session and is out, and he is not on the numbers' missing list, so Orban and Esteve are expected to pair at the back; Ouedraogo and Guiu are still out (counted). For Lens, right-back Ruben Aguilar and Michael Cuisance (ill) are out, Chavez is not registered and Edouard is still injured (Cuisance and Edouard counted), while Gradit, Ivanovic and Bulatovic are back in the squad. Three French outlets expect a back three with Ganiou and Abdulhamid wide, Haidara and Titraoui in midfield and Thauvin, Hazard and Sima in attack. Slovak referee Ivan Kruzliak, a little below average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, already adding about 8% to Leipzig for their recent scoring and taking a little off Lens for Cuisance and Edouard. Lukeba's absence is confirmed today but is not in the numbers, so a reshuffled Leipzig back line faces a Lens front three of Thauvin, Hazard and the returning Sima. A small nudge up: 3.5 x 1.03, about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, split fairly evenly, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Lens are expected in a back three with a centre-back, Ganiou, at left wing-back and Aguilar out on the right, so they look less of a crossing side, while Leipzig still go wide through Nusa and Raum. That balances out, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Leipzig's quieter recent record (-8%) and Ivan Kruzliak's slightly low card rate (-5.4%) counted. Both sides need the win and Demichelis expects a strong reaction from Lens after the Como defeat, but there is no history of bad blood and no ban in play, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots, adding about 7% to Leipzig for their busy recent shooting and trimming Lens (-9%) for their low count. Lens lose Cuisance and Edouard but get Sima back up front, and Leipzig miss Lukeba at the back rather than any attacker, so the volume of shooting should look like the numbers expect. I stay at 28.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target and already add about 15% to Leipzig for how often they have tested goalkeepers lately. The one thing they cannot see is Lukeba's absence, which should make it a little easier for Lens to get shots away cleanly, so a slight nudge: 11.5 x 1.02, about 11.7.

401915298.overall: Real Madrid are 2nd on a perfect 12 points under Jose Mourinho and have won nine in a row, the last 2-1 against Celta; Vinicius starts (his domestic ban does not apply in Europe) and Valverde and Tchouameni return after being rested. Rodrygo and Endrick are out (counted), Asencio is injured, Mendy is not registered, and Dumfries, though in the squad list, missed Monday's training and is not expected to play; most previews have Guler and Bellingham starting, one has Brahim in. PSV are 24th on 4 points and lead the Eredivisie, but Mauro Junior is out (counted) with 18-year-old Noah Fernandez expected to replace him, Dest is a doubt and Schouten, Nagalo, Plea and Ouaissa remain out. Norwegian referee Espen Eskas, an average carder, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say a high 4.5 goals, built on Madrid's strong recent scoring and PSV's open style under Bosz, and they already take a little off PSV for Mauro Junior. Madrid's front line of Mbappe, Vinicius and Bellingham is expected to start, and PSV keep their attack of Perisic, Mijnans, Van Bommel and Til, so nothing new changes the picture. I stay at 4.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners and already trim PSV (-6%) for their low recent count against strong defences. Valverde back at right-back adds width for Madrid and Perisic and Van Bommel give PSV wide threat, which is their normal shape and already in the records, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, close to both teams' usual rates, and include Espen Eskas, whose record is about average. A young PSV midfield with Fernandez in for the captain may have to foul to stop Madrid's runners, but that is a guess, there is no needle between the clubs and no ban in play, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots, including Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+4.8%). Mourinho talked of rotating, but today's previews still have Bellingham, Guler or Brahim, Vinicius and Mbappe behind a first-choice midfield, while PSV are a little weaker in midfield without Mauro Junior. Nothing is big enough to move, so I stay at 31.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.7 on target, with Madrid's sharp recent finishing counted (+8%). Mbappe and Vinicius both start and PSV keep their usual attacking set-up, possibly without Dest at right-back, which is roughly what the numbers assume, so I stay at 12.7.

401915297.overall: Slovan Bratislava are bottom of the league phase with no points and a 1-17 goal record after 12 straight European defeats, though they beat Ruzomberok 1-0 on Saturday under Yaya Toure. Slovan are without Suleiman Camara (counted, a big cut to their goals), Mustafic and Medvedev, with Wimmer, Gajdos and Cerepkai doubtful. Betis are 11th on 9 points and 4th in La Liga after a 1-1 derby draw with Sevilla; Ceballos and Morante are out (counted), Lo Celso is out with a knee knock from training, and Pellegrini is expected to make seven or eight changes before Saturday's game with Rayo, with Parrott up front and Cucho only fit for minutes off the bench. French referee Jerome Brisard, about average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already cut Slovan's share hard (about -37%) for Camara's absence, so I do not count that again. What they cannot see is Betis's heavy rotation: seven or eight changes, Lo Celso out, Parrott leading the line and Cucho only off the bench. A small trim: 2.9 x 0.96, about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Betis around 6.1 and their busy recent corner counts already in (+3%). Even a rotated Betis should dominate the ball with Antony, Abde or Riquelme on the wings while Slovan defend deep, which is already in both records, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, reflecting Slovan's usual card rate when chasing the ball, and Jerome Brisard's about-average record is already counted. Betis are a technical side, the game has no history and nothing points to more heat than usual, so I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots and add about 11% to Betis for how much Slovan concede. A Betis side with seven or eight changes and no Lo Celso may play at a lower tempo once ahead, and Slovan's own shooting at this level has been thin with Gajdos doubtful. A slight trim: 31.8 x 0.97, about 30.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, including a 6% boost for Betis and already a lower Slovan figure without Camara. Betis start with second-choice attackers such as Parrott and Riquelme, and Slovan rarely test goalkeepers in this competition, so I go to 10.5 x 0.96, about 10.1.

401915378.overall: Sabah are 30th of 36 with 3 points in their first Champions League campaign and Barcelona 8th with 9, so Barcelona need the win to stay in the top-eight race, at the Olympic Stadium in Baku. Barcelona are without Lamine Yamal (ankle, kept at home as a precaution), Rodri, Christensen, Espart and Bardghji, and a team-news page today lists Kounde and Olmo as doubts; the numbers count Yamal, Christensen and Espart only. Flick said Cubarsi can play if needed and previews expect a rotated side with Gavi or Bernal, Fermin, Adeyemi and Gordon around Raphinha and Pedri. Sabah lose centre-back Aden McCarthy to a red-card ban (counted) and leading scorer Simic is a doubt; one team-news page says Mickels is banned for yellow cards while another predicted line-up still starts him, so that stays unclear. Scottish referee Nick Walsh, who shows a lot of cards, is in charge and the numbers already add about a quarter to cards for him; line-ups were not out when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.4 goals (1.1 Sabah, 3.4 Barcelona), already taking off Yamal (-16.7%), Espart and Christensen for Barcelona and McCarthy for Sabah, and counting both sides' good scoring runs. What they can't see is Flick's rotation, Olmo and Kounde being doubts, and Sabah's top scorer Simic (and possibly Mickels) missing, so I trim a little, to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 6.6 of them for Barcelona, who should have most of the ball against a Sabah side that likes to play out from the back but will spend long spells defending. Without Yamal the width comes from Adeyemi and Gordon with Cancelo pushing on, so play still goes down the flanks, and the changes are mostly in defence and midfield, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already adding Nick Walsh's high card rate (+26%; about five yellows a game in his two games this season) and Sabah's busy recent card record (+11%), and taking a little off for Barcelona's quieter run. That is already a high figure for a game with no rivalry and nothing new on discipline turned up, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots (8.9 Sabah, 25.6 Barcelona), lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting. Yamal is one of Barcelona's main shooters and the numbers take his absence only off goals, Flick is rotating with Olmo doubtful, and Sabah may lack Simic up front, so I lean lower, to about 33.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, 9.0 for Barcelona, already lifted for their recent accuracy (+8.5%). Without Yamal and with a rotated side the quality of Barcelona's chances should dip a little, and Sabah's attack is thinner if Simic misses out, so I trim to about 11.8.

401915293.overall: Slavia are 34th of 36 with 1 point and Villarreal 29th with 3, so both are below the top-24 line and need a win; Villarreal coach Inigo Perez called it decisive and blamed Saturday's 3-2 loss at Barcelona, after leading 2-0, on mentality. Slavia are without Sturm, Chaloupek, Pitak, Ouanda and Ogbu, all counted (Sturm alone takes about a quarter off their goals), and two previews today add midfielder David Moses injured and Lukas Provod a doubt, which the numbers don't list; neither preview has striker Chory in the side. Villarreal miss Saliba (ankle surgery) and Diatta, both counted, while Gerard Moreno is back in the squad and Foyth and Akhomach are back in training; the earlier report of Mourino being banned is not backed today, with both predicted line-ups starting him. Perez called Slavia the most aggressive side in the competition, and Slovenian referee Rade Obrenovic, with a slightly low card record, is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals (0.9 Slavia, 2.4 Villarreal), already cutting Slavia hard for Sturm and the other injured players. Moses out and Provod doubtful thin Slavia's attack further, but Gerard Moreno's return gives Villarreal an extra option the numbers don't count, so I lean only slightly lower than before, to about 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, fairly even (4.1 Slavia, 5.1 Villarreal), with Slavia's recent corner run counted. Slavia play a direct, wing-back game and must attack at home, Villarreal go wide through Buchanan and Moleiro, and the absences change little here, so I stay at 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, taking a little off for Obrenovic's slightly low card record and Slavia's calmer recent run. Perez expects Slavia's usual aggression and both sides need the win, but that intensity is part of Slavia's long record the numbers already use, and the Mourino ban did not hold up, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted for Slavia's heavy recent shooting (+15.9%). With Moses out and Provod doubtful, Slavia lose two midfielders who shoot and create, which the numbers can't see, so I trim to about 30.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target, with Slavia's recent accuracy counted (+11.3%). A thinner Slavia midfield points to slightly fewer good chances, partly offset by Gerard Moreno's return for Villarreal, so I lean a touch lower, to about 9.9.

401915291.overall: Atletico Madrid (26th, 4 points) and Viking (25th, 4 points) sit one place apart in the clubs' first meeting, and Atletico, after losing to Liverpool and Bayern, need to win at home to keep any hope of the top eight. Atletico beat Getafe 3-0 on Sunday; Lookman and Cuti Romero are out and counted, Marc Pubill has recovered from his ankle sprain according to two Spanish reports, Hjulmand is back from his European ban, and one report says Sorloth was left out of the squad, with Kang-in Lee or Baena next to Julian Alvarez. Viking, three points behind Bodo/Glimt in the Norwegian title race after losing 3-2 at Tromso, miss Bjorshol, D'Agostino, Roseth and Baertelsen (counted), and an illness has hit the squad: left-back Kristoffer Haugen is out and top scorer Peter Christiansen is still a doubt, neither on the numbers' list. Lugano's club and Swiss media reported on Wednesday that Albian Ajeti's ban is domestic only, so he can play here, while the numbers still take him out as suspended (about -16% on Lugano's goals); match-day checks (UEFA's match page and others) found nothing that changes that, and line-ups were not out at writing. goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals but take about 16% off Lugano's scoring for Ajeti as suspended, while Swiss reports say his ban covers only domestic games and he is free for Thursday. I add most of that back, to about 3.3, but not all of it, as Croci-Torti has said he will rotate with a league game on Sunday and Jablonec have been hard to score against at home in Europe.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.4 for Jablonec, who need a first European win and attack with crosses at home, with both sides' recent corner counts already in. Ajeti's return changes Lugano's finishing rather than how much of the ball they have, and a few rotated players should not change their wide play, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already adding about 6% for referee David Smajc (6.0 a game in two on record) and more for both sides' recent bookings. Ajeti's red card was in the Swiss league and these clubs have never met, so nothing points to an unusually heated game and I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, a fairly open game, already lifted a little for Jablonec's recent volume. Ajeti's return helps Lugano's finishing more than their number of shots, and the rotation expected before Sunday pulls slightly the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Jablonec's stand-in keeper Mihelak (Hanus is counted) and Ajeti's availability matter more for how many go in than for how many are on target, so I stay at 9.2.

401915739.overall: A Baltic meeting in Kaunas between Kauno Zalgiris, last of 36 with 0 points and a 1-11 goal record (0-4 at Brighton, 1-4 at home to Brann, 0-3 at Lugano), and Riga FC, 19th-20th after three 1-1 draws. Riga's long-term absentee Varslavans is already counted and referee Daniyar Sakhi (confirmed, 3.0 cards in one game) is in the numbers; match-day line-up news was thin again, so the view rests on earlier reports and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already trim Zalgiris for scoring 3 in their last six. Riga come in after three straight 1-1 draws and a coaching change days ago, and a tired Zalgiris side at the end of their season has scored once in three European games, so I trim a little to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, 4.9 for Zalgiris at home, already trimmed for their few recent corners. Reports expect Riga to keep their attacking style under Zanetti rather than change shape, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already cutting Riga for only 2 cards in their last three and taking a little off for referee Daniyar Sakhi's low record. It is a Baltic meeting but not a real rivalry, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, already lifting Riga (47 shots in their last three) and trimming Zalgiris. Zalgiris' fatigue and the long break could slow the game, but they need a first point at home and say they expect to be the stronger side, so I stay at 27.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target and already cut Zalgiris for only 4 on target in their last three. With no new injuries reported on either side and only Varslavans out (counted), I stay at 8.5.

401915809.overall: Two sides near the bottom on 1 point each: Pafos are 31st and Midtjylland 34th, so both need a win to stay in the play-off race, and Sa Pinto has called the three points essential. Midtjylland lead the Danish league and play the title clash at Copenhagen on Sunday; Mike Tullberg has said the Conference League comes second because of their injury list, and keeper Bakker, Diao, Castillo, Watjen, Billing and others are on the numbers' list. Referee Ishmael Barbara's low card rate is already in the numbers, and match-day checks found no line-ups or further news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and now already take about 19% off Pafos for Lele's ban, which my earlier view had added by hand, so I drop that part. Winger Ngamaleu is still out without being in the numbers and Midtjylland are set to rotate before Copenhagen, so I trim a little to about 2.5; a weakened Midtjylland defence keeps it from going lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, already lifted for both sides' recent corner counts. Pafos lose two wide attackers in Lele and Ngamaleu but Midtjylland's tall side brings set pieces either way, and the two pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already low because both sides have been booked rarely lately and referee Ishmael Barbara shows 3.3 a game. There is nothing heated between these clubs, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent volume. Lele's ban mainly hits finishing and is now counted on goals, but Pafos are also without Ngamaleu and a rotated Midtjylland, who have put Europe second, tend to create less, so I go to about 26.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target, with Pafos at 5.7 after 26 on target in their last six, a run Lele and Ngamaleu helped build. The numbers count Lele only on goals, so with both wide attackers missing and a changed Midtjylland side I go to about 9.5, a smaller cut than this morning.

401915808.overall: Brann are 6th-7th with 7 points and unbeaten in nine games in all competitions, scoring in each, so a home win would put them close to the top eight; they won a wild 4-3 at KFUM on Sunday. Their long injury list (Tronstad, Sorensen, Kjartansson, Gudmundsson, Opsahl, Boakye) is already in the numbers. AGF are 24th on 2 points with one goal in three European games, but have won their last two league games; Yakob, Tingager, Poulsen and Serra are out (counted), and Jacob Andersen's hand knock against Lyngby has not been reported as keeping him out. Referee Antoniou Menelaus is already counted. News was thin: match-day checks turned up no new team news, so this view rests on earlier Danish reports and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 1.8 for Brann, and already count Brann's 16 goals in six and the absences of Gudmundsson and Sorensen. AGF have scored once in Europe but concede regularly away from home, which fits the numbers' split, and nothing new is out on either side, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers expect 11.7 corners, with Brann's 40 corners in six already adding 8% and AGF's few recent corners trimming theirs. Brann attacking at home for a top-eight place fits that picture rather than adding to it, so I stay at about 11.7.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.8 cards, 2.3 of them for AGF, with their recent card rate and referee Antoniou Menelaus already counted. These clubs have never met and a full away end adds noise rather than needle, so I stay at about 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, 18.5 for Brann, already lifted 10% for Brann's recent volume and cut for AGF's. AGF's two league wins came with a near-full side and nothing new keeps anyone out, so I stay at about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target and already lift Brann (34 on target in six) and trim AGF (8 in three). Brann's side at KFUM was close to their best available, so nothing new moves it and I stay at about 10.4.

401915506.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) meet Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, where UEFA moved the game for security reasons; most of the crowd should still be Besiktas fans. The trip went badly: bad weather stopped the team plane landing in Batumi, it diverted to Rize and the squad finished the journey by road on Wednesday evening, and Vincenzo Italiano's press conference was cancelled. Fanatik reports Italiano plans to limit Vlahovic's and Trossard's minutes before the Galatasaray derby, with Hyeon-gyu Oh and Vaclav Cerny set to start; Umit Akdag is banned, Agbadou stayed home with a swollen knee and Miretti is still out. Hapoel are without first-choice keeper Ofir Marciano, Lucas Ventura and Dan Biton (all counted) and play a league game two days later. Danish referee Morten Krogh's low card rate is already in the numbers; I trim goals and shots on target a little more than yesterday because Besiktas' best finishers now look likely to start on the bench; a last check of starting11 shortly before kick-off lists the same absences (Akdag banned, Miretti injured, Agbadou not involved; Ventura and Biton out for Hapoel, who may rotate with a league game two days later), and no confirmed line-ups were out yet, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 2.3 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.2%) and for Marciano missing in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%). Since yesterday Fanatik reports Oh and Cerny should start with Vlahovic and Trossard kept fresh for the derby, and the squad arrived late after a diverted flight and a road trip, neither of which the numbers can see, so I go a little lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should still have most of the ball against a side near the bottom of the table, and changes up front alter who finishes moves more than how often they reach the byline, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh's low card rate (2.9 a game). Krogh's crew was also diverted by the weather and came in by road from Trabzon, but he is still the named referee, and with a mostly Besiktas crowd and a home side expected to dominate nothing points clearly up or down, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas, already nudged for recent form. Besiktas should keep shooting often against a weak defence with a reserve keeper, but a rotated front line after a tiring journey may take a little off their volume, so I go slightly lower, to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, 7.7 for Besiktas, already lifted for sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and trimmed for Hapoel (-5.8%). With Vlahovic and Trossard, Besiktas' best finishers, now expected to start on the bench, the quality of their chances should drop a little, so I go to about 10.0.

401915519.overall: Celta (27th, 3 points) host Bournemouth (2nd, 12 points from four wins) at Balaidos, with Claudio Giraldez under pressure after Celta scored very little lately. Borja Iglesias and Carl Starfelt again stay out of the squad, Hugo Gonzalez has a thigh strain (counted) and Miguel Roman is still out, so Iago Aspas or Pablo Duran should lead the attack; Iglesias' absence already shows in Celta's poor scoring. Giraldez said Celta cannot manage minutes and will field their most competitive side, while Bournemouth miss Alex Toth, Julian Araujo and Juanlu Sanchez (all counted), with Kroupi not registered and Evanilson likely up front. Both sides play league games three days later, and German referee Harm Osmers books a little more than average, which the numbers count. A last check of starting11 before kick-off lists the same absences plus Celta's Moriba as doubtful with a knee problem (one source only), and David Brooks back in Bournemouth's squad; line-ups were not out yet, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 1.2 for Celta and 1.8 for Bournemouth, and already trim Celta for scoring only 4 in their last 6 (-4.2%). Iglesias, Celta's main striker, is confirmed out again and the numbers don't list him, but Starfelt's absence at the back helps Bournemouth's Evanilson-led attack, so I stay only mildly lower, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, split fairly evenly. Giraldez wants a high tempo with Celta's wing-backs pushing on, and Bournemouth play direct and wide on the break; recent corner form is already in the numbers, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already raised 14% for referee Harm Osmers (4.5 a game) and lowered for Bournemouth's few recent bookings. Bournemouth's aggressive press can cause fouls, but that is part of their record, and there is no rivalry here, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and already raise Celta for shooting a lot lately (+8.3%), even if few go in. Celta without Iglesias still shoot often from range, Giraldez promises his strongest side and Bournemouth's front line is close to full strength, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 on target and already cut Celta's share for poor accuracy (-9.6%), which largely reflects playing without Iglesias. Bournemouth keep their side up with Evanilson available and Kroupi not registered, so I stay at about 8.7.

401915517.overall: Dinamo Zagreb (9th, 7 points) host Bayer Leverkusen (7th, 9 points) at the Maksimir, both chasing a top-eight place; Dinamo won 2-0 at Sunderland last time, Leverkusen lost 1-0 at home to Marseille. Dinamo miss Scott McKenna and Robert Mudrazija (both counted), with captain Josip Misic expected to start and Dion Beljo, scorer of four of their five European goals, up front. Leverkusen miss Martin Terrier and Kennet Eichhorn (counted), Boniface and Oermann are not registered, and Diaby, Tella and Kofane only returned with short league cameos; Tella starred off the bench in the 4-0 over Paderborn, while Guela Doue's return is still open. Both sides play league games three days later, and Ukrainian referee Mykola Balakin shows few cards, which the numbers already take off. Nothing new since yesterday moves any stat, so I stay with the numbers; a last check before kick-off: starting11 still lists Kofane, Tella, Diaby and Maza as doubtful for Leverkusen and expects rotation with league games three days later, which supports keeping the numbers rather than going higher.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.1 of them for Leverkusen. Leverkusen's attack is close to full strength with Diaby, Tella and Kofane back, though some may only play part of the game, and Schick should lead it as before; McKenna's absence already shows in Dinamo's record, so I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.3 for Leverkusen, who have won a lot of corners lately (already counted, +1.5%). Leverkusen should have most of the ball while Dinamo play direct and quick in transition through Beljo, the pattern their recent games already show, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already take 17% off for referee Mykola Balakin, who averages 2.8 a game. The Maksimir crowd can raise the temperature in a game both sides need, but that is part of Dinamo's home record, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots and already lift Leverkusen for heavy recent shooting (+6.2%). Both sides may manage minutes with league games right after, but Leverkusen's deeper squad, which sporting director Rolfes says they want to use to win here, means changes should not cut their volume, so I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 on target and already lift Leverkusen (+6.6%) after 45 on target in their last six. With the absences on both sides already in the missing list and Misic fit for Dinamo, I stay at about 10.

401915507.overall: Marseille (31st, 3 points) host Levski Sofia (10th, 7 points) at the Velodrome and need a win to keep play-off hopes alive; OM won at Leverkusen last time in Europe but then lost 3-2 at home to Le Mans from 2-0 up, and Genesio spoke of a mental and defensive fragility. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is back in the group after illness, while Emerson and Derek Cornelius remain out (both in the numbers). Sportal confirms Serginho, Levski's key midfielder, missed training before the flight and will not play, along with long-term absentees Kirilov and Sangare; only Kirilov is in the numbers' missing list. Only 500 Levski fans are allowed in, and Montenegrin referee Nikola Dabanovic books a little more than average, which the numbers count. I keep a slight lean lower on goals and shots on target for Levski's weakened attack; a last check before kick-off: starting11 still lists Hojbjerg as doubtful with illness, while Le Phoceen reported him back in the group; line-ups were not out yet, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 2.5 for Marseille and 0.8 for Levski, and already lift Levski a little for Emerson's absence. Levski are confirmed without Serginho, their main creator, who is not in the missing list, which trims their small share, and Hojbjerg's return steadies Marseille after the Le Mans collapse, so I go mildly lower, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 6.9 for Marseille. Levski like the ball at home but away they usually end up defending deep, which pushes corners Marseille's way; that and both teams' lower recent corner counts are in the numbers already, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already raised 9% for referee Nikola Dabanovic (4.6 a game), lifted for Marseille's recent bookings and lowered for Levski's. A Marseille side under pressure could get frustrated, but nothing concrete points that way and the away end will be tiny, so I stay at about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, 18.7 for Marseille, already trimmed for their lower recent shot count (-6.9%). Marseille need the win and should have long spells of pressure, while Levski without Serginho may shoot a little less, but they rarely shoot much away anyway, so I stay at about 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 on target, 7.2 for Marseille, and already trim Marseille for poor recent accuracy (-6.7%). Levski's attack loses Serginho, which takes a little off their 2.9, so I go slightly lower, to about 10.0.

401915521.overall: Olympiacos are 6th in the Europa League with 10 points and unbeaten in five European games; AC Milan are 28th with 3 points and need a win in Piraeus to get back towards the play-off places, though they arrive after a 5-1 league win over Frosinone. Leon Bailey is out with a hamstring strain (Greek and Italian outlets), which the numbers do not know; Olympiacos also miss Chiquinho, Hezze, Puerta, El Kaabi and Yazici, all counted. Milan are without Modric, Pavlovic, Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze and Terracciano, and Camarda pulled up on the eve of the trip, leaving Goncalo Ramos as the only recognised striker; Tomori is back on the bench and Il Milanista expects Maignan, Jashari in midfield and Pulisic and Ramos up front, as Amorim has no room to rotate. English referee Chris Kavanagh's card record is already counted (about +20%). My leans stay small: slightly fewer corners and shots without Bailey, slightly more cards because Milan must chase; no confirmed line-ups were out at the last check before kick-off, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals (1.0 Olympiacos, 1.1 Milan), already cut for Chiquinho and Hezze and for Modric, and nudged up for both sides' recent scoring. Bailey's absence is not in the numbers, and Milan now have only Ramos as a true striker after Camarda's injury; Pavlovic missing at the back works a little the other way, so I trim only slightly, to about 2.06.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.9 corners, 5.3 for Olympiacos, already adding for their busy wide play (+7.8%) and taking off Milan's low recent count. Without Bailey, Olympiacos lose one of their main wide outlets, something the numbers can't see, so I go a bit lower, to about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, adding about 20% for referee Chris Kavanagh's record and trimming a little for both sides' calm recent games. The referee is counted, so I don't size him again; my small lean to about 5.1 is for the stakes, with a depleted Milan needing a win in a full, loud Karaiskakis and Olympiacos chasing a top-eight place.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.7 shots, 15.3 for Olympiacos and 9.4 for Milan, already adding for Olympiacos' busy attack (+9.5%) and cutting Milan for their thin recent output (-16%). Bailey's absence takes some threat from Olympiacos, while Milan chasing the game works the other way, so I go slightly lower, to about 24.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, with Milan's lower recent accuracy already taken off. Pulisic and Ramos lead Milan's threat with no real cover behind them, while Olympiacos lose Bailey, one of their most accurate shooters, and rely on Gelson, Jota Silva and Gonzalez, so I trim a little to about 8.0.

401915520.overall: RB Salzburg are 26th with 4 points and want 'clearly three points' against Ararat-Armenia, who are last with no points and 14 goals conceded in four games. Salzburg lost at Austria Wien on Sunday and must make up for top scorer Haris Tabakovic (meniscus surgery, out for the rest of the year), with Karim Konate expected to lead the line. The numbers take off Tabakovic, Redzic and Kitano and also count Schmid, Boma, Mellberg and Omoregie, but Redzic and Morgalla are listed only as doubtful, not ruled out, while Veratschnig is still out. Ararat play without banned first-choice keeper Joao Bravim (counted); stand-in Arman Nersesyan went off injured early in their last league game but is expected to start. Only about 8,000 tickets were sold, and Dutch referee Lawrence Visser's high card rate is already counted; a last check of starting11 before kick-off lists the same Salzburg absences (Tabakovic, Kitano, Schmid, Boma, Mellberg, Veratschnig) and Bravim banned for Ararat; line-ups were not out yet, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, 1.5 for Salzburg, after taking about 19% off each for Tabakovic, Redzic and Kitano and adding for Ararat's missing first-choice keeper. Redzic is still a doubt rather than ruled out, and Ararat's reserve keeper Nersesyan carries a knock from the weekend, so the numbers may cut Salzburg a little too hard; I go slightly higher, to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.4 corners, 5.2 for Salzburg. Previews expect Ararat to sit deep and Salzburg to attack down the wings with Lindstrom and Vertessen, the pattern the numbers already assume, and losing a central striker changes who finishes moves more than how often they reach the byline, so I stay at about 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, adding about 27% for referee Lawrence Visser's 6.2 cards a game and a little for Ararat's busy recent card count. Both are already counted; a quiet, two-thirds-empty stadium and a home side expected to dominate the ball give no reason to go higher or lower, so I stay at about 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.5 shots, 18.7 for Salzburg, already adding for their busy recent attack (+8.5%). Against a bottom side with a reserve keeper Salzburg should still have the ball and shoot often even without Tabakovic, and Rohl has asked for many more chances, so I stay at about 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, adding about 10% for Salzburg's sharp recent shooting; their missing players only change the goals number, not this one. Much of that accuracy came through Tabakovic, and without him in Vienna Salzburg made few clear chances, so I trim slightly to about 9.9.

401915508.overall: Union Saint-Gilloise are 4th in the Europa League with 10 points, unbeaten in 16 games in all competitions and top in Belgium; they host this game at Den Dreef in Leuven. Lech Poznan lead the Polish league but have 1 point from four European games (2 scored, 12 conceded) and need a win. This morning's checks found no new absences: Lech travelled with Sayyadmanesh back in full training and new keeper Johnsson, while Pablo Rodriguez stays in Spain for rehab and captain Ishak is still training only on his own; one squad-news page still lists Sayyadmanesh with a groin problem, so his minutes are uncertain. Union have Sylla and Kricfalusi back in training but miss Havenaar, Mac Allister and Biondic (all counted) plus reserve keeper Chambaere. Spanish referee Jose Maria Sanchez Martinez's card record is already in the numbers, so with nothing new pointing either way I keep the numbers; a last check of starting11 before kick-off now lists Sayyadmanesh as out with a groin problem along with Ishak and Rodriguez, which fits Lech's blunt recent attack the numbers already show; the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, 2.5 for Union, with Biondic's absence already taken off and Havenaar's added for Lech. Lech's attack has played without Ishak and Pablo Rodriguez for weeks, which their recent scoring already shows, and Sayyadmanesh's return is offset by doubts over his fitness, so I stay at about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.3 corners, already trimming Union for their low recent corner count (-7.5%). Lech are expected to sit in a cautious 4-2-3-1 and are short of wide players with Walemark out, but their small share (3.1) already reflects that, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, adding about 20% for referee Sanchez Martinez's record and lowering for both sides' calm recent games. Lech need points but are a passing side, Union control games, and a modest crowd at Den Dreef adds little heat, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers expect 30.9 shots, with Union expected to dominate (21.5). Both clubs play league games three days later and some rotation is possible, but Lech's line-up has barely changed lately and Union get Sylla back, so the one-sided game the numbers assume still fits and I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 shots on target, already adding for Union's accurate recent shooting (+11.2%). Lech's blunt attack without Ishak and Pablo Rodriguez is what their recent games already show, and Kevin Rodriguez is expected to lead Union's line as usual, so I stay at about 11.7.

401915518.overall: Benfica top the Europa League with four wins from four and want to secure a top-eight place; Viktoria Plzen are 30th with 3 points but have won four of their last five games, and Radoslav Kovac says almost his whole squad is fit. Benfica's 24-man squad (Record, A Bola) leaves out Prestianni (lower back pain) and Aursnes (thigh, close to a return), neither of which the numbers know, plus Barreiro, who is already counted; young right-back Banjaqui travels. Marco Silva still has Pavlidis, Lukebakio, Rafa Silva, Sudakov, Schjelderup and Jhon Duran, and Plzen miss only Jemelka (counted). Croatian referee Igor Pajac has a very low card rate, which the numbers already take off, and a frosty night is expected in Plzen on a pitch said to be in excellent shape. No new news this morning, so I keep the small trim on Benfica's attack for Prestianni; no new absences turned up at the last check before kick-off, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.9 for Benfica, already nudged up for their scoring run and down for Barreiro. Prestianni, who scored on Sunday, stayed in Lisbon with back pain and the numbers don't know it; Benfica still have Pavlidis, Lukebakio and Rafa Silva, so I trim only slightly, to about 2.6.
