cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add for both teams' busier recent bookings and for Stegemann's slightly above-average record (4.1 a game). Hütter wants more pressing and intensity, but this is a race for Europe rather than a grudge match, so I stay at about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots and already raise Frankfurt by about 20% because Stuttgart allowed 117 shots in their last six, much of that while Stiller was out. With Stiller and Jaquez back, Stuttgart tired after Inter, and Uzun doubtful for Frankfurt, I trim slightly to about 29.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already lifting Frankfurt 10% for their recent accuracy and trimming Stuttgart for poor finishing. Stuttgart managed one on target at Inter and look short of sharpness, and Uzun may miss out for Frankfurt, so I take a little off, to about 10.7.

401883104.overall: Eibar (7th, 24 points from 14, level with the last play-off place) host Burgos (5th, 27 points) at Ipurua on Saturday in a meeting of two promotion play-off hopefuls. Eibar have won one of their last five league games and lost 2-1 at Girona last time, while Burgos have three wins in five, the latest 1-0 at home to Albacete. Eibar's club note lists Elijah Gift, Juan Bernat and Imanol García de Albéniz outside the group, none of them a regular scorer; Burgos are without David González (counted by the numbers), striker Jon Karrikaburu (out since late October, so already in their recent form) and Brais, who had nose surgery. Both have Copa del Rey ties next week (Eibar v Sant Andreu, Burgos v Zaragoza) but neither coach has hinted at rotation for this game, and no referee is named yet; match-specific news was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.8 goals, already taking about 11% off Burgos for David González and a little more for six tight past meetings. Karrikaburu is also out, but Burgos have scored 9 in six without him, which the momentum figure counts, and Eibar's absentees are a full-back and squad players rather than their scorers Guruzeta and Iván Gil, so I stay at 1.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already adding about 9% to Burgos for their 37 corners in six games and taking a little off Eibar's low recent count. Bernat, now listed outside the group, would have given Eibar width on the left, but he has been out for a while and that is in their recent figures, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Burgos are one of the more booked sides (40 yellows, no reds) and Eibar the less booked (28 yellows), and the numbers already raise Burgos for Eibar's opponents collecting cards lately. No referee is named yet and there is no derby edge, so I stay at about 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.6 shots, already raised for both sides' busy recent shooting (Eibar 96 in six, Burgos 89). Neither side is expected to rotate before next week's cup ties, and Burgos coach Sergio Francisco says they will not change their game for the opponent, so I stay at about 25.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target, with about +12% already on Burgos for their 30 on target in six. Eibar's forwards appear fit and Burgos' missing strikers are already reflected in their recent form, so nothing points either way and I stay at 8.1.

401875531.overall: Leaders PSV (29 points from 13) host Go Ahead Eagles (9th, 17 points) four days after a 5-1 defeat at Real Madrid in the Champions League, where they led through an Ivan Perisic penalty before collapsing after the break; Peter Bosz called it 'a bad half'. In the league PSV have won their last three by four goals or more (7-0, 6-2, 4-1), and they are without Mauro Junior, Schouten, Plea, Ouaissa and Nagalo, all in the numbers. One injury list rates Perisic a 25% doubt after he left the pitch in Madrid, but Sports Mole's preview lists him in the expected XI and no club news confirms a problem, so I give it little weight. Go Ahead have scored once in their last three league games after 2.3 a game before that, miss Saathof and Marsman, and have Dean James and Linthorst (and, per one list, Margaret) as doubts; Tengstedt is their main threat. Dennis Higler's low card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, 3.1 for PSV, already trimmed for Mauro Junior and Plea and for Go Ahead's quieter attack lately. I trim slightly to about 4.2 for the Tuesday trip to Madrid, which the numbers have no congestion adjustment for; I have dropped most of my earlier Perisic worry because only one injury list has him as a doubt and Sports Mole expects him to start.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners, about 7 for PSV as they pin opponents back. Go Ahead may be without wide players Dean James and Margaret and are weaker away, which fits the deep approach the numbers already expect, so I stay at about 11.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards, already lowered about 12% for Dennis Higler, who shows 2.1 cards a game. PSV rarely need to foul at home and Go Ahead's bookings are close to normal, and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at about 2.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.2 shots, 24.6 for PSV. I trim slightly to about 33.2: PSV come off a draining night at the Bernabeu four days earlier, which the numbers do not count, though their league lead and home form keep Bosz from resting many, so it stays a mild lean.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target, 8.0 for PSV. The same Madrid fatigue points slightly lower, to about 11.7; Go Ahead's own attack has gone quiet (one goal in three) but leans on Tengstedt, and the numbers already count their recent shooting.

401885393.overall: Académico de Viseu (6th, 20 points) host Alverca (11th, 12 points) at the Fontelo after the international break. Bruno Pinheiro's Viseu won six in a row before losing 1-0 at Nacional, no injuries or bans have been reported for them, and Pinheiro praises Alverca's technical quality and high pressing. Sérgio Ferreira's Alverca are out of the cup and without a league win since mid-October; A Bola (23-24 Nov) says right-sided defender Nabil Touaizi has a calf relapse and may not play again this year, Meupiyou and Abdulai are still recovering from knee surgery and Rayan Lucas is doubtful with a knee problem, while internationals Bojang, Chissumba, Merheg and Camara are back. The numbers count Meupiyou, Abdulai and Raveyre but not Touaizi or Rayan Lucas (both from A Bola only). Vítor Ferreira (Braga FA) referees; his record is not in the numbers. News on Viseu was thin, so the view stays close to the numbers with a small trim on corners.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, with Meupiyou and Abdulai already taken out for Alverca. Alverca's attack has gone quiet in recent rounds and Rayan Lucas is a doubt, but their back line is also short with Touaizi out, which the numbers don't know, and Pinheiro says Viseu often come from behind at the Fontelo; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners, with Alverca taking the larger share (5.0) against a Viseu side that conceded 40 in its last six (already counted). I trim a little, to about 8.0, because Alverca lose Touaizi on the right flank and possibly Rayan Lucas, neither in the numbers, which should take something off their wide play; A Bola is the only source for both, so the trim stays small.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already adding a little because Viseu have been booked more than usual lately (19 in their last six). Vítor Ferreira was named referee, but I found nothing on his card record and the numbers have not used one; Alverca's high press could bring some fouls, yet there is no rivalry or special stakes, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, with Alverca shooting more (14.8) after an 11% boost for their recent volume. Their absences are mostly in defence and midfield, the returning internationals give them their usual front line, and Viseu's squad is fit, so I see no reason to move it and stay at 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Viseu's forwards, led by André Clóvis, have been accurate this season and Alverca's finishing has dipped, both already in the recent form the numbers count; with no new absences in attack confirmed (Rayan Lucas is only a doubt), I stay at 9.1.

401874977.overall: Third-placed Inter (29 points, three behind Lazio, won all six home league games) host Genoa (10th, 16 points, four wins in five under Daniele De Rossi, three clean sheets in five) on Saturday evening; the numbers make Inter clear favourites. Cristian Chivu's side beat Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League on Wednesday and have three days' rest; one preview says rotation is saved for the coming Coppa Italia tie between the same sides. Calhanoglu and Bonny are out and Zielinski is doubtful (the numbers take all three off, about -16% on Inter's goals), Lautaro is fit again, and one report has Bastoni as a doubt after a knock. Genoa lost Lorenzo Colombo for the season (counted), and Osmajic (6 goals) leads the line. Referee Giovanni Ayroldi averages 5.7 cards a game, which the numbers already count; news for this match was thinner than usual (two outlets).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.9 for Inter, already taking off Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny (about -16%) and Colombo for Genoa. Zielinski is listed as doubtful rather than out by two previews, and Lautaro is back, but Genoa have kept three clean sheets in five under De Rossi; these roughly balance, so I stay at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.7 for Inter, already raised for Inter's 42 corners in six and lowered for Genoa's 20. Inter's wing-backs Dimarco and Spence drive most of their corners whoever plays in midfield, and Genoa sit in a back three, so nothing new points either way; I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards: referee Giovanni Ayroldi shows 5.7 cards a game and the numbers already add about 53% for him, while cutting both sides for their quiet recent records (Genoa 7 cards in six). Genoa are clear of the relegation zone and this is no derby, so I add nothing on top of the referee and stay at about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, already lifted for Inter's heavy recent shooting (+9%). The missing players only move the goals, not the shots: without Calhanoglu and probably Zielinski, Inter lose their main long-range shooters, with Sucic in the playmaker role, three days after Stuttgart. One preview says rotation will come in the cup instead, so the lean stays small, about 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target, 6.3 for Inter. For the same reasons as shots (Calhanoglu out and Zielinski doubtful, a short turnaround after the Champions League) I go a little lower to about 8.9; Genoa's attack without Colombo, a part-time starter, changes little, with Osmajic in form.

401876391.overall: A relegation fight on Saturday evening: Le Havre (18th, 2 points, the only side without a win, seven straight league defeats) host Strasbourg (16th, 10 points, six defeats in seven). Both have new coaches who lost their first game: Valerien Ismael at Le Havre (3-1 at Troyes), who wants an aggressive pressing side, and Vitor Matos at Strasbourg (1-0 at home to Brest), who now talks about defending better first. Le Havre lose Enzo Koffi to a red-card ban and have a long injury list (Mpasi, Zagadou, Mambimbi, Pembele, with Nakamura, Ndiaye and Mosengo doubtful); Strasbourg are without Panichelli, Balde, Oso and now midfielder Essugo, while Alsa'Sports reports Giovanni Reyna fit again after Matos' press conference, which Sports Mole does not yet have and the numbers do not assume. Geoffrey Kubler referees (5.0 cards a game in a small sample, already counted); the pressure of a must-win game for two struggling sides is the main thing the numbers cannot see.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 1.4 for Le Havre and 1.5 for Strasbourg, and they take about 11% off Strasbourg for Reyna's absence. Alsa'Sports, which follows the club closely, says Reyna is fit again (one report; Sports Mole still lists him out), and Le Havre have conceded 25 in eleven; against that Matos is stressing defence, so I lean only a little higher, 2.9 to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners, with both sides winning slightly fewer than usual lately, which the momentum already reflects. Le Havre are expected in a 3-4-2-1 with wing-backs and Strasbourg in their usual 4-2-3-1 with Yassine and Nanasi wide, so nothing on tactics changes the picture and I stay at about 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already lifted about 7% for referee Geoffrey Kubler and counting both sides' recent cards, but they have no stakes flag for this game. It is a bottom-of-the-table meeting with two new coaches desperate for a first win, Le Havre already had Koffi sent off last week and Ismael wants hard pressing, so I lean a little higher, 4.1 to about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, already boosted because Le Havre have been shooting a lot lately (96 in six) even while losing. Strasbourg's missing forwards (Panichelli, Balde) have been out for weeks and are in their form, and Matos' more careful approach could offset a returning Reyna, so I stay at 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target, about level between the sides. Both defences are weakened by long-term injuries that the recent numbers already show, and Strasbourg losing Essugo in midfield is a small change in either direction, so I stay at about 9.

401876390.overall: Promoted Le Mans (13th, 11 points) host Lille (3rd, 21 points, the fewest goals conceded in the league) on Saturday evening. Davide Ancelotti's Lille beat Bayern Munich 2-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday, three days before this game, so some rotation is likely; striker Ayase Ueda scored in that game, so the earlier report of him being out was wrong. Lille are without Tiago Santos (season), Hamza Igamane and Tanguy Nianzou, and Le Mans miss Sidibe and Bourabaa, with Colas and Yohou doubtful per one report; the numbers already take about 16% off Le Mans' goals for Bourabaa and some off Lille for Santos. Le Mans come in after a 3-2 comeback win at Marseille but have conceded in all eleven league games. Mathieu Vernice referees, a strict one at 4.5 cards a game, and the numbers already add about 20% for him; I lean only slightly lower on Lille's attack for the Bayern game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, 1.4 of them for Lille, and they already take off Santos and Le Mans' Bourabaa. Ueda is fit after scoring against Bayern, so my earlier reason for going lower is gone, but a changed Lille side three days after a big Champions League night may be a bit less sharp, so I lean slightly lower, 2.2 to about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Both sides win few corners (Le Mans about 3.2 a game, Lille 3.9), which is already in their ratings, and Le Mans' wing-back system with Calodat and Buades is how they have played all season, so I stay at about 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, already raised about 20% for referee Mathieu Vernice (4.5 a game) and trimmed because Lille have drawn and given few cards lately. Le Mans have been booked often (17 in six), which is counted too, and there is no rivalry, so I stay at about 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.3 shots and already take some off for Lille's quieter recent run (66 shots in six). Rotation after Bayern is likely (Lille have kept 73% of their XI over six games), so I lean slightly lower, 23.3 to about 22.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, 4.4 of them for Lille. Ueda leads the line, but tired legs or a changed supporting cast after Bayern should make Lille a little less clinical than usual, so I lean slightly lower, 8.2 to about 8.0.

401876388.overall: Nice (7th, 17 points) host promoted Troyes (14th, 11 points, one point above the play-off place) on Saturday evening. Olivier Pantaloni's Nice lost 3-2 at home to PSG last weekend after three straight wins, while Stephane Dumont's Troyes have taken six points from their last three after five straight defeats, including a 3-1 comeback at Le Havre. Nice are missing Antoine Mendy, Laurent Abergel and Moise Bombito, with Abdelmonem doubtful; Sports Mole calls top scorer Elye Wahi doubtful but expected to play (one report). Troyes are without forward Yacouba Kone and defender Paolo Gozzi, with Ifnaoui facing a fitness test (one report); none of these absences is new or a main scorer, so they are largely in the form already. Aurelien Petit referees (2.4 cards a game in five games, counted), neither side plays in Europe and news was thin (two outlets), so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Nice, who have scored 14 in their last six and have won the last three meetings. Wahi is a slight doubt but expected to start, Nice's patched defence has been patched for weeks, and Troyes' loss of Kone is minor with Mille their top scorer, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, slightly more for Troyes, and momentum already trims both sides a little. Nice play wing-backs (Clauss, Nkounkou) and Troyes see little of the ball, but the numbers already know both styles, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards: pushed up because Nice have had 17 cards in their last six, then trimmed about 11% for referee Aurelien Petit, who has shown only 2.4 a game. There is no rivalry or discipline news, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.9 shots, already trimmed because Troyes have allowed few shots lately and Nice have shot less than usual. Both sides are expected to field settled line-ups with no European or cup game around it, so I stay at about 23.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, 4.6 for Nice. Nice's attack is intact if Wahi plays and Troyes' defence has been tight lately (18 on target allowed in six), both already in the numbers, so I stay at about 8.

401876387.overall: Leaders PSG (1st, 26 points, five straight league wins) host Lorient (10th, 16 points) on Saturday evening, three days after a 2-2 home draw with Roma in the Champions League. Doue and Kvaratskhelia are out for the season and the numbers already take them off; the earlier report that Dembele and Marquinhos were out is wrong, as Dembele came on and won a penalty against Roma and both are pushing to start (Paris Supporters), while young Longoni is injured. Luis Enrique often rotates after European nights and his lineup is not known before Friday's press conference. Alexandre Dujeux's Lorient miss Katseris, Fadiga, Bamba and Isaak Toure (counted) and drew 1-1 with Rennes last time; the last two meetings were draws. Bastien Dechepy referees (4.4 cards a game, already counted); I lean slightly lower only on PSG's shot volume.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 1.9 for PSG, lifted by their hot run and trimmed for Doue and Kvaratskhelia. I had leaned lower for rotation, but Dembele is fit and pushing to start, which balances a changed side after Roma, so I now stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.6 for PSG. Even a rotated PSG side keeps the ball and pushes Lorient back into their 3-4-2-1, so the corners stay one-sided as the numbers already expect; I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards: PSG have picked up only 3 cards in their last six, then the numbers add about 16% for referee Bastien Dechepy (4.4 a game). There is no rivalry and nothing at stake beyond the points, so I stay at about 3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, already lifted for PSG's busy recent run. Three days after Roma, Luis Enrique is likely to change several players and PSG may manage the game once ahead, so I lean slightly lower, 26.6 to about 25.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, PSG's share lifted for an unusually sharp run (48 on target in six). A partly rotated front line after a Champions League night is unlikely to keep that pace fully, so I lean slightly lower, 9.8 to about 9.5.

401882789.overall: Second-placed Real Madrid (33 points, five straight wins, every home game won this season) host Alavés (9th, 16 points, unbeaten in three but without an away league win) on Saturday night; the numbers make Madrid strong favourites with about 3.2 goals. José Mourinho's side beat PSV 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday and have away games at Real Sociedad, Athletic and Arsenal next, so previews expect some changes (Konaté and Huijsen in defence, Carreras or Cucurella at left-back, Güler or Bernardo Silva). Rodrygo and Endrick are out and counted by the numbers; Raúl Asencio is also out, but he has been for weeks, so recent games already reflect it. Quique Sánchez Flores's Alavés miss Mikel Rodríguez, Facundo Garcés and Hugo Novoa (counted) and, new this week, Benavídez, with Guevara and Youssef Enríquez doubts; Goal expects a compact 3-5-2. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.5 for Madrid, already raised for their 18 goals in the last six (+3.5%). Mbappé (17 goals in 17), Vinícius and Bellingham keep the attack strong even with some rotation, and Alavés's five-man defence aims to keep it tight; Rodrygo and Endrick are already counted. Nothing new moves it, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already lowered because Alavés have won few corners lately and Madrid concede few. A deep Alavés block can give Madrid corners, but Madrid prefer to attack through Vinícius and Mbappé rather than cross, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, 2.8 for Alavés, already lowered for Madrid's quiet recent record. Alavés may rest Rebbach, one booking from a ban, and sit deep, which brings some fouls, but that is their usual game and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, already raised for Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+7.2%). Rotation after PSV and before three away games may take a little off, but Madrid's depth and a home game against a side that defends deep keep their output high, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, already lifted for Madrid's sharp recent finishing (47 on target in six). Benavídez's absence for Alavés is in midfield and changes little in front of goal, so I stay at about 10.2.

401875530.overall: Promoted SC Cambuur (8th, 18 points) host Sparta Rotterdam (14th, 12 points) on Saturday night at the Kooi Stadion, and the numbers expect a high-scoring Cambuur win, about 4.7 goals. Cambuur won 3-2 at FC Utrecht last time but have taken only 7 of their 18 points at home; Amofa is out for the season and Berkhout is a doubt, while the brief's other day-to-day absences (Asselman, Visser, Meijster, Westerhof) were not confirmed by the pages I read. Rogier Meijer's Sparta have lost four of their last five, most recently 1-5 at home to AZ, and have conceded two or more in 11 straight games; captain Bruno Martins Indi is banned and keeper Brouwer (Bednarek deputises), Quintero and Verschuren are out, all counted by the numbers. Martin van den Kerkhof's low card record is already counted. News for this game was thin (Sports Mole and an injury list) and nothing I found adds to what the numbers see, so every stat stays where the numbers put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.7 goals, 3.1 for Cambuur, already raised for Cambuur's 18 goals in six, Sparta's 17 conceded in that run and the absences of Martins Indi, Brouwer and Verschuren. Sparta's 11 games in a row conceding twice or more fits that picture, while Cambuur's modest home record (7 points of 18) pulls the other way and is part of their home rating, so I stay at 4.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, fairly even (4.5 for Cambuur, 5.0 for Sparta), with only a small trim for Cambuur's recent corners. Sports Mole expects both sides in their usual shapes, with Cambuur's front three of Ceka, El Arguioui and Hamache behind Binder, so nothing changes the count and I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards and already count Martin van den Kerkhof's low record (2.4 a game over 33 games, -24.7%) and Sparta's busy recent bookings (+11.7%, Martins Indi's two yellows against AZ among them). Sparta are under pressure near the bottom, but nothing points to a heated game beyond that, so I stay at about 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, 15.3 for Cambuur, with small momentum changes already in (+3.1% for Cambuur, -4.7% for Sparta). Both expected lineups are close to those of recent weeks, and Sparta's changes are the ones the numbers already know, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target, already raised for Cambuur's sharp recent shooting (39 on target in six, +11.8%) against a Sparta side that keeps conceding. Berkhout's doubt is too unclear to move, so I stay at 11.3.

401883100.overall: Fran Escribá's Real Valladolid (12th, 19 points) host Real Sociedad B (19th, 13 points, in the drop zone) at Zorrilla on Saturday night, with Valladolid favourites. The Sanse lose Álex Marchal and Gorka Carrera, two of their front three, to bans after the 0-3 home defeat to Cádiz (counted by the numbers), and EFE's list also has Iñaki Rupérez banned for yellow cards, which the numbers do not count. Valladolid's striker Juanmi Latasa is now confirmed back: Escribá said he is 'perfect' and trained well, and the club says he has rejoined the group, while the numbers still take him out (-7.6% on Valladolid's goals). Trilli (adductor) and Guille Bueno (not registered until January) are out; Escribá says he will play his best side here despite the Copa derby against Zamora on Wednesday. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, 1.5 for Valladolid, after taking 7.6% off their goals for Latasa and 6.8% off the Sanse's for Carrera's ban. Two sources now say Latasa is fit and trained fully, so that deduction is out of date; he may not play the whole game after injury, so I give back most of it, +4% on the total, about 2.6. The Sanse's extra absence, Rupérez, does not suggest they will score more.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.0 for Valladolid, already raised for both sides' busy recent corner counts (40 for Valladolid in six). Escribá wants a pressing side that makes the Sanse uncomfortable, which fits how the numbers already see the game, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, raised a little for the Sanse's recent bookings, including the two second-yellow reds against Cádiz and Rupérez's fifth yellow. A young side fighting relegation away from home can pick up cards, but the numbers already see their record and no referee is named, so I stay at about 6.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, already lifted 14% for the Sanse's busy recent shooting against a Valladolid defence that has let opponents shoot a lot (93 in six). Without Marchal and Carrera the Sanse front line is weaker, but both bans are counted, and Latasa's return changes who shoots for Valladolid more than how often, so I stay at about 28.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already raised for Valladolid's sharp recent shooting (40 on target in six). With Latasa, their first-choice striker, confirmed fit after missing the Celta Fortuna game, I add a little, +3%, about 9.4.

401885385.overall: Two struggling sides meet in Guimarães on Saturday night: Tiago Margarido's Vitória (14th, 9 points) are three games without a win and went out of the cup 0-2 at home to Braga, while Estrela (12th, 10 points) have lost five league games in a row but won their first game under new coach Pepa, 1-0 at Portimonense in the cup, with their first clean sheet in 13 games. Pepa returns to a club he used to coach. Vitória's defence is hit: centre-back Toni Borevkovic is suspended after his fifth booking and left-back João Mendes has torn a cruciate ligament, so with Francisco Dias also out a youth player (Kebdani or 18-year-old Tomás Rodrigues) is likely at left-back and Thiago Balieiro at centre-back; the numbers list Dias but not Borevkovic or Mendes. For Estrela, Arévalo is doubtful (in the numbers) and Sports Mole says Eddy Doué and Béni Souza have been left out lately for disciplinary reasons and are doubts. Cláudio Pereira referees, with his record (5.7 cards a game in 3 games) already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Vitória and 0.9 for Estrela. Vitória's back line has lost Borevkovic (suspended) and João Mendes (season over), neither of which the numbers know, so a new centre-back and an untested youth left-back should give Estrela's attack, led by five-goal Antonetti, a little more. Wind's fitness doubt and Vítor Carvalho's injury are from one report and matter little next to Braga's other forwards, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.6 for Braga after an 8.1% boost for their recent corner count, and take 6.5% off Casa Pia for their few lately. Braga will have most of the ball against a Casa Pia side that has sometimes sat deep, which is what the numbers expect, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already taking 6% off for António Nobre's low record and a little off Braga, who have been booked less than usual lately. There is no rivalry here; Casa Pia chasing a first home point could add a few fouls, but nothing in the news is strong enough to move it, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots and add 27% to Braga for a very high recent volume (114 shots in six, including a 4-0 European win). I trim a little, to about 24.4, because this is Braga's third game in ten days with a Thursday night in between, Vítor Carvalho is reported out of midfield, and a run that far above their usual level tends not to hold fully against a side defending deep.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target, 5.0 for Braga after a 6.8% boost for recent accuracy, and 3.0 for a Casa Pia side whose forwards are not scoring. My small shot trim is mostly about Braga's speculative volume, not their good chances, so I stay at 8.0.
